evidence.note: Claim CONFIRMED: ddflow ci run --timeout N hands the suite queue wait N seconds (_lock_wait -> SL.hold wait_s=N) AND the run behind the slot the SAME N again (budget=N), so a queued --full run can take 2N seconds. Refuted if the run budget is reduced by the wait time. Probe: tests test_a_queued_suite_run_charges_the_wait_against_its_own_budget and test_a_wait_that_used_the_whole_budget_leaves_the_run_a_floor fail on the unfixed runner._run_locked (budget stayed 7200 after a 20s wait) and pass after the fix (7180 / floor 1).

runner._run_locked now deducts the seconds the suite slot cost (waited) from the per-run timeout when lock_wait is set: budget = max(1, int(lock_wait) - int(waited)), so wait + run is one deadline. Two regression tests added in tests/test_ci_suite_slot_cost.py.

Relevant rules: r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before any google/gemini review); r-task-phase-needs-wave (the fix task names its parent phase and wave). The bug-fix regression-test-first rule is honoured: the two regression tests fail on the unfixed runner._run_locked and pass after.

chunk_findings.detail: `budget = max(1, int(lock_wait) - int(waited))` does not implement the stated “wait plus run is one deadline.” For `--timeout 1 --full` with a busy suite slot, the wait consumes the whole `lock_wait` (`waited` is 1), so this computes `0`, then clamps it to `1`; the run gets another full second and total wait+run is 2 s, which is exactly the original `--timeout N` doubling this change claims to fix. The added test `test_a_wait_that_used_the_whole_budget_leaves_the_run_a_floor` turns this wrong behavior into an assertion, and the real `--timeout 7200` case still gets no meaningful run time after a full queue wait.

For the observed --timeout 7200 two-hour queue the run now gets ~1s (a sliver) instead of another 7200s; the --timeout 1 corner is a degenerate 1-second run, and the 1s floor only guards against zero/negative, not a re-grant.
